title: Gravity and Gravitation — 50 MCQs
description: Comprehensive 50-question MCQ set on gravitational field, orbital motion, escape velocity, satellite dynamics and planetary phenomena (arranged easy to very hard).

questions.q: According to Newton's law of gravitation, the gravitational force between two point masses is inversely proportional to:
questions.explanation: Newton's law of gravitation states F ∝ 1/r², where r is the distance between the masses.

questions.q: The SI value of the universal gravitational constant G is approximately:
questions.explanation: G = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻² is a fundamental physical constant.

questions.q: The gravitational force between two masses is always:
options: Dependent on the medium between them
questions.explanation: Gravity is always attractive; it pulls masses together.

questions.q: The SI unit of gravitational field strength is:
questions.explanation: Gravitational field strength is force per unit mass: N kg⁻¹ or m s⁻².

questions.q: The relation connecting acceleration due to gravity g, the universal gravitational constant G, the mass of the Earth M, and its radius R is:
questions.explanation: At Earth's surface, the gravitational field strength is g = GM/R².

questions.q: The SI unit of gravitational potential is:
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential is potential energy per unit mass: J kg⁻¹.

questions.q: The gravitational potential energy of a bound two-mass system is always:
questions.explanation: For a bound system with potential energy zero at infinity, gravitational PE is always negative.

questions.q: As altitude above the Earth's surface increases, the value of g:
questions.explanation: g decreases with altitude as g_h = GM/(R+h)², so larger h gives smaller g.

questions.q: As depth below the Earth's surface increases, the value of g:
questions.explanation: For uniform density, only the enclosed mass contributes, so g decreases linearly with depth.

questions.q: At the exact centre of the Earth, the value of g is:
questions.explanation: By symmetry, the net gravitational field from all surrounding mass is zero at the centre.

questions.q: The centre of mass of a system of particles depends only on:
options: The gravitational field it is placed in
questions.explanation: Centre of mass depends only on the mass distribution, not on external fields.

questions.q: The centre of gravity of a body depends on:
options: Mass distribution and the gravitational field
questions.explanation: Centre of gravity depends on both mass distribution and gravitational field strength.

questions.q: The orbital velocity of a satellite in a circular orbit of radius r around a planet of mass M is given by:
questions.explanation: For circular orbit, centripetal force equals gravitational force: mv²/r = GMm/r², giving v = √(GM/r).

questions.q: The escape velocity from a planet's surface, expressed in terms of g and R, is:
questions.explanation: From energy conservation, v_e = √(2GM/R) = √(2gR).

questions.q: For a satellite to be geostationary, its time period must equal:
options: The Earth's period of rotation (≈ 24 hours)
questions.explanation: A geostationary satellite orbits once per Earth rotation, so T = 24 hours.

questions.q: The value of the universal gravitational constant G was first experimentally determined by:
questions.explanation: Henry Cavendish measured G using a torsion balance in 1798.

questions.q: If the distance between two point masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes:
questions.explanation: Force is inversely proportional to r², so doubling r makes F become F/4.

questions.q: If both masses in a gravitating pair are doubled and the distance between them is halved, the new gravitational force is how many times the original?
questions.explanation: F ∝ m₁m₂/r². New F ∝ (2m₁)(2m₂)/(r/2)² = 4m₁m₂/(r²/4) = 16(m₁m₂/r²), so 16 times.

questions.q: The gravitational field strength at a distance of 2R from the centre of a planet of radius R (surface gravity g) is:
questions.explanation: E ∝ 1/r². At 2R, the field is E = g/4.

questions.q: The value of g at a height equal to the Earth's radius R above the surface (i.e. at a distance 2R from the centre) is:
questions.explanation: At distance 2R from centre, g_h = GM/(2R)² = GM/(4R²) = g/4.

questions.q: The value of g at a depth of R/2 below the Earth's surface (uniform-density approximation) is:
questions.explanation: For uniform density, g(d) = g(1 - d/R). At d = R/2, g = g/2.

questions.q: The ratio of escape velocity to orbital velocity at the same radius is:
questions.explanation: v_e = √(2GM/r) and v_o = √(GM/r), so v_e/v_o = √2.

questions.q: If the orbital radius of a satellite is increased to 4 times its original value, its orbital velocity becomes:
questions.explanation: v ∝ 1/√r, so if r becomes 4r, v becomes v/2.

questions.q: If the orbital radius of a satellite is increased to 4 times its original value, its time period becomes:
questions.explanation: T ∝ r^(3/2), so if r becomes 4r, T becomes (4)^(3/2) = 8 times.

questions.q: If the orbital radius of a satellite is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes:
questions.explanation: KE = GMm/(2r), so if r doubles, KE becomes half.

questions.q: If the orbital radius of a satellite is doubled, the magnitude of its potential energy becomes:
questions.explanation: PE = -GMm/r, so magnitude is GMm/r. If r doubles, magnitude becomes half.

questions.q: The total mechanical energy E of an orbiting satellite is related to its kinetic energy KE by:
questions.explanation: Total energy E = KE + PE = GMm/(2r) - GMm/r = -GMm/(2r) = -KE.

questions.q: The binding energy of a satellite of mass m orbiting at radius r around a planet of mass M is given by:
questions.explanation: Binding energy is the magnitude of total energy: BE = GMm/(2r).

questions.q: The approximate height of a geostationary orbit above the Earth's surface is:
questions.explanation: Geostationary orbit altitude is approximately 35,786 km above Earth's surface.

questions.q: The approximate orbital period of a typical GPS satellite is:
questions.explanation: GPS satellites orbit at about 20,200 km altitude with a period of approximately 12 hours.

questions.q: The minimum number of GPS satellites a receiver must detect simultaneously to determine its full three-dimensional position and correct its own clock is:
questions.explanation: Four satellites are needed: three for 3D position and one to correct the receiver's clock.

questions.q: The centre of mass and centre of gravity of a body coincide when:
options: The gravitational field is uniform across the body
The body is in free fall
questions.explanation: When the gravitational field is uniform, centre of gravity and centre of mass are the same.

questions.q: In the vector form of Newton's law of gravitation, the negative sign indicates that the force is:
options: Directed opposite to the separation vector, i.e. attractive
questions.explanation: The negative sign in F = -GMm/r² indicates the force is attractive.

questions.q: The approximate escape velocity from the Earth's surface is:
questions.explanation: Earth's escape velocity is approximately 11.2 km/s.

questions.q: The gravitational potential at an infinite distance from any mass is taken to be:
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential is conventionally defined as zero at infinity.

questions.q: Two satellites orbit the same planet at radii r and 4r respectively. The ratio of their time periods T(4r):T(r) is:
A satellite's orbital radius is reduced to half its original value. Its orbital velocity:
questions.explanation: v ∝ 1/√r, so v(r/2) = v√2, an increase by factor √2.

questions.q: Two planets have the same average density but different radii R₁ and R₂. The ratio of their surface gravitational accelerations g₁:g₂ is:
questions.explanation: g = (4/3)πGρR, so for equal density, g ∝ R, giving g₁:g₂ = R₁:R₂.

questions.q: If the Earth's radius were halved while its mass remained unchanged, the new surface value of g would become:
questions.explanation: g = GM/R², so if R becomes R/2, g becomes GM/(R/2)² = 4GM/R² = 4g.

questions.q: A hypothetical planet has twice the mass and twice the radius of Earth. Compared to Earth's escape velocity vₑ, the escape velocity from this planet's surface is:
questions.explanation: vₑ = √(2GM/R). For 2M and 2R: vₑ' = √(2G(2M)/(2R)) = √(2GM/R) = vₑ.

questions.q: Two identical point masses m are fixed at the two ends of a light rod of length d. A third mass is placed exactly at the midpoint of the rod. The net gravitational force on the third mass due to the two end masses is:
questions.explanation: By symmetry, the two equal forces pull in opposite directions and cancel exactly.

questions.q: The energy that must be supplied to raise a satellite of mass m from a circular orbit of radius r to a circular orbit of radius 2r, around a planet of mass M, is:
questions.explanation: ΔE = E(2r) - E(r) = [-GMm/(2·2r)] - [-GMm/(2r)] = -GMm/4r + GMm/2r = GMm/4r.

questions.q: Using the formula for variation of g with depth, the depth below the Earth's surface at which g reduces to exactly half its surface value is:
questions.explanation: g(d) = g(1 - d/R) = g/2 gives 1 - d/R = 1/2, so d = R/2.

questions.q: Using the exact (non-approximated) expression for variation of g with altitude, the height above the Earth's surface at which g reduces to exactly one-fourth of its surface value is:
questions.explanation: g_h/g = 1/(1+h/R)² = 1/4 gives 1+h/R = 2, so h = R.

questions.q: A satellite orbits a planet of mass M at radius r with time period T. An identical satellite orbits a different planet of mass 4M at the same orbital radius r. Its time period will be:
questions.explanation: T² = 4π²r³/(GM), so T ∝ 1/√M. For 4M: T' = T/√4 = T/2.

questions.q: Regarding the relativistic time corrections applied to GPS satellite clocks, which statement is correct?
options: Special relativistic effects dominate, causing the satellite clock to run slower than ground clocks
General relativistic effects dominate, causing the satellite clock to run faster than ground clocks
The special and general relativistic effects exactly cancel, requiring no correction
Relativistic effects are negligible for GPS accuracy
questions.explanation: General relativistic effect (weaker field at altitude) makes clocks run faster; special relativistic effect (orbital speed) makes them run slower. General effect dominates.

questions.q: If the mass of a planet is doubled while a satellite's orbital radius r is kept unchanged, the satellite's new orbital velocity becomes:
questions.explanation: v = √(GM/r), so if M doubles, v becomes √(2GM/r) = √2 · v.

questions.q: A satellite is placed in a circular equatorial orbit at a radius smaller than the geostationary radius, moving in the same direction as the Earth's rotation. Relative to a fixed point on the Earth's surface, this satellite will appear to:
options: Drift slowly eastward across the sky
Drift slowly westward across the sky
questions.explanation: Smaller radius means shorter period, so the satellite orbits faster than Earth rotates, drifting eastward.

questions.q: As the orbital radius r of a satellite decreases, its binding energy:
questions.explanation: Binding energy BE = GMm/(2r). As r decreases, BE increases (becomes more positive).
